Situation.Name: Sixteen Columns, One Deck
Situation.Setting: A darkened measurement hall. Sixteen tall, narrow translucent glass columns stand in a row receding into haze, evenly spaced, each the height of two people. Every column contains the identical vertical stack of eight small glowing intent cards — the SAME eight cards, in the SAME order, repeated in all sixteen columns. What differs is how far up each column the cards are lit: one column at the far left is lit all the way to the top, one column is entirely dark with its eight cards visible but cold and grey, and the rest are lit to scattered intermediate heights, forming a jagged, non-monotonic skyline. Faint numeric readouts float at the base of each column.
Situation.Camera: Wide shot, low three-quarter angle looking along the row of columns so the varying lit heights read as an uneven skyline. Subject stands in the right third in the foreground, turned three-quarters away from camera toward the columns. Negative space and haze across the upper left for text overlay.

CharacterPose.Expression: Focused analytical concentration, slight squint, mouth set — the look of someone reading a distribution she built the instrument to produce, and finding it disagrees with itself
CharacterPose.BodyPosition: Standing close to the row, weight settled, shoulders squared to the columns
CharacterPose.Gesture: One hand resting flat against the glass of a SHORT, barely-lit column in the foreground — deliberately not the tall bright one, which stands further down the row untouched

Article.Name: Sixteen identical card stacks
Article.Description: Sixteen tall glass columns, each holding the same vertical stack of eight small glowing cards in the same order — visibly, unmistakably the same deck repeated sixteen times
Article.Application: Fill the middle and left of frame, receding into haze
Article.SymbolicMeaning: One slice of guidance, read by sixteen different models

Article.Name: The uneven lit skyline
Article.Description: The fill height of each column varies wildly and without pattern — full, near-empty, mid, dark, high, low — deliberately NOT a smooth ascending or descending progression
Article.Application: The dominant visual rhythm across the row
Article.SymbolicMeaning: The same records are worth wildly different amounts, and not in order of capability

Article.Name: One wholly dark column
Article.Description: A single column whose eight cards are present but entirely unlit, cold grey, no glow at all
Article.SymbolicMeaning: A model that read the guidance and changed nothing

Article.Name: Floating interval brackets
Article.Description: Small thin horizontal error-bar brackets hovering beside each column's readout, some narrow, some wide enough to cross zero
Article.Application: Faint, at the base of the columns, secondary to the skyline
Article.SymbolicMeaning: Every rate carries a width; a single trial is an anecdote

Environment.Name: Darkened measurement hall
Environment.Description: Matte black floor and walls with the columns' light reflecting in long streaks across the floor
Environment.Application: Surrounds the scene, keeps all light sourced from the columns

KeyDetails: The eight cards must read as IDENTICAL from column to column — same shapes, same order, same positions. Only the lit height differs
The lit heights must be jagged and unordered, never a neat ascending staircase
Exactly one column is completely unlit while its neighbours glow
Her hand rests on a short, dim column, not on the tallest one
Her attention is on the column she is touching, not on the brightest in the row
Situation.LightingFocus: Cool cyan and electric blue dominant, sourced entirely from the lit card stacks. The tall fully-lit column throws the strongest glow from further down the row, while the short column under her hand gives only a weak magenta-tinged underlight across her fingers and jaw — the composition should make the eye ask why she is touching the dim one

ArticleContext.Title: What Sixteen Models Did With the Same Eight Principles
Themes: the value of a guidance slice is not a property of the slice
lift is not monotonic in model capability
needing guidance and being able to act on it are different axes
measuring this is mostly a fight against your own instrument

CompositionNotes.Framing: Wide shot along a receding row of columns to show the full uneven skyline
CompositionNotes.SubjectPlacement: Character in the right third foreground, columns filling the middle and left
CompositionNotes.DepthOfField: Shallow to medium; far columns softened by haze but their lit heights still legible
CompositionNotes.TextSafeArea: Upper left haze reserved for text overlay
